missing_capabilities.name: ftp_bounce_active_probe
missing_capabilities.description: RFC 959 Section 5.2 PORT command lets client name an arbitrary host:port for the data connection. Historic FTP bounce (CVE-1997-0163 class; nmap ftp-bounce): send PORT with a non-client IP/port and issue LIST/RETR — a permissive server proxies TCP connects to arbitrary internal hosts, turning it into an internal port scanner and firewall-bypass relay. Module never issues PORT and never checks whether the server rejects non-client PORT targets. High ROI: converts one FTP box into a pivot for the entire adjacent subnet.

missing_capabilities.name: site_cpfr_cpto_active_probe
missing_capabilities.description: CVE-2015-3306 / CVE-2019-12815 mod_copy detection is banner-only and only matches 'ProFTPD 1.3.[0-5]'. Many vulnerable installs strip or reformat the banner, and CVE-2019-12815 was a re-break with different affected ranges. An active probe — issue SITE HELP and look for CPFR/CPTO, or attempt SITE CPFR /etc/passwd → check response — would confirm exploitability regardless of banner. Same for SITE EXEC (wu-ftpd class), SITE CHMOD, SITE INDEX.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 959 SITE; ProFTPD mod_copy; CVE-2015-3306 / CVE-2019-12815

missing_capabilities.name: pasv_internal_ip_leak
missing_capabilities.description: 227 response to PASV encodes the server-chosen data-channel IP: '227 Entering Passive Mode (10,0,0,5,196,3)'. A server bound behind NAT frequently returns its RFC1918 address, disclosing internal topology (dual-homed hosts, DMZ layout, container IPs). Module never issues PASV/EPSV. Feed the leaked internal IP as an additional host fact.

missing_capabilities.name: auth_tls_actually_negotiate
missing_capabilities.description: Module only checks FEAT for 'AUTH TLS' text. Doesn't send AUTH TLS and complete the handshake, so cannot detect: (a) advertised-but-broken TLS, (b) accepted SSLv3/TLS1.0/weak ciphers, (c) expired/self-signed/wildcard/hostname-mismatch cert, (d) CCC (Clear Command Channel) permitted post-AUTH which downgrades back to cleartext, (e) PROT P / PBSZ not enforced so data channel stays cleartext despite AUTH TLS on the control channel. RFC 4217 Sec 4/9.

missing_capabilities.name: credential_brute_force_and_defaults
missing_capabilities.description: Only 'anonymous' is tried. No sweep of vendor defaults (ftp:ftp, admin:admin, root:root, user:user, guest:guest, cisco:cisco, tomcat:tomcat), no password-spray, no reuse against known_credentials facts. FTP is one of the classic brute-force targets and this module skips it entirely. Should also try the SITE-derived usernames and any usernames emitted by known_users.

missing_capabilities.name: cwd_user_enumeration_differential
missing_capabilities.description: Wu-FTPd / older ProFTPD leak valid usernames via response differential to CWD ~user or USER <name> before PASS (530 vs 331 timing/text differences). Module doesn't probe. When it finds a valid user, feed to known_users.

missing_capabilities.name: implicit_ftps_990
missing_capabilities.description: is_ftp() only matches port 21 or service name containing 'ftp'. Implicit FTPS on TCP 990 (starts TLS immediately, no AUTH command) is not detected as an FTP target, so no cert collection, no cleartext-vs-encrypted comparison, no cross-referencing with plaintext 21.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 4217 Appendix A; historical implicit FTPS

missing_capabilities.name: help_and_stat_and_site_help_fingerprint
missing_capabilities.description: HELP and SITE HELP reveal full command sets (identifies vendor even when banner is stripped/faked, and enumerates dangerous SITE verbs — EXEC, CHMOD, CPFR, INDEX, WHO, ZONE). STAT with no argument returns server state including current transfers, uptime, and sometimes connected users. Module issues neither.

missing_capabilities.name: anon_write_during_passive_probe
missing_capabilities.description: prove_writable exists but only runs when analyze() explicitly calls it with the anon creds — the credfree probe() never tests write. An anonymous-writable FTP root is one of the most common footholds (upload → web-shell / poisoned firmware bundle) and should be tested on every anon success automatically, then emitted as a critical finding.

missing_capabilities.name: recent_vendor_cves_missed
missing_capabilities.description: Banner map covers only vsftpd 2.3.4, ProFTPD 1.3.3c, and ProFTPD mod_copy. Missing: CrushFTP CVE-2024-4040 unauth VFS escape + template RCE (banner 'CrushFTP'); CrushFTP CVE-2023-43177; SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2021-35211 pre-auth RCE (banner 'Serv-U'); Serv-U CVE-2024-28995 path traversal; ProFTPD CVE-2019-12815 mod_copy unauth; ProFTPD CVE-2020-9273 UAF; ProFTPD CVE-2023-51713; FileZilla Server CVE-2023-48795 (Terrapin); Pure-FTPd CVE-2019-20176 DoS; vsftpd 3.0.3 privesc chain; WS_FTP CVE-2023-40044 pre-auth RCE. These are the FTP CVEs currently used by ransomware crews.

missing_capabilities.name: cwd_directory_traversal_probe
missing_capabilities.description: CWD / , CWD .., CWD /etc, CWD C:\ — some misconfigured jails let the client escape the chroot. Module never probes. A successful traversal to /etc or /root is a critical-severity file-disclosure primitive; the subsequent RETR /etc/shadow feeds hashes into the credentials sink.

missing_capabilities.name: tls_cert_collection
missing_capabilities.description: When AUTH TLS succeeds, the server certificate CN/SAN, issuer, notBefore/notAfter, and fingerprint are prime hostname/domain sources. Module never collects the cert, so hostnames sink never receives them and known_hostnames/domains stay empty on TLS-fronted FTP.

missing_capabilities.name: mirror_content_hash_extraction
missing_capabilities.description: Runbook says 'mirror the tree for offline secret hunting' but nothing in the module actually retrieves anything or scans the retrieved files. When anon-readable, the module should pull well-known loot filenames (backup.tar, config.xml, web.config, .git/config, id_rsa, wp-config.php, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, sam._, ntds.dit) and hand extracted hashes/creds to the hashes and known_credentials facts. This is where FTP feeds the rest of the toolchain.

missing_capabilities.name: syst_and_banner_os_hint
missing_capabilities.description: SYST reply and 220 banner ('UNIX Type: L8', 'Windows_NT', 'AIX') carry a clean OS identifier that feeds host os_hint and downstream service selection. probe() captures syst but analyze() only stashes it on the target dict — never emits it as an os-fingerprint fact.

missing_capabilities.name: eprt_epsv_ipv6
missing_capabilities.description: RFC 2428 EPRT/EPSV — IPv6-capable data channel negotiation. Module ignores it; on v6-only or dual-stack targets the module can miss the entire session establishment path and EPSV can leak the v6 address the server advertises for data.

missing_capabilities.name: port_command_bounce_guard_check
missing_capabilities.description: Even when active bounce fails (server enforces the same-client-IP rule from RFC 2577), the module could report on the enforcement state — servers that accept PORT 127,0,0,1,... but not third-party IPs still enable localhost-only attacks against services bound to loopback. Distinguish 'bounce-blocked', 'bounce-loopback-only', 'bounce-anywhere'.

cross_service_wire_gaps: anon-success should emit anonymous:anonymous (and the actual PASS token used) into known_credentials as a confirmed working credential — currently the fact never leaves the module
SYST + 220 banner carry a clean OS hint ('UNIX Type: L8', 'Windows_NT', 'AIX') that should feed the host os_hint sink but is only kept on the target dict
220 banner often contains an admin email (root@host.example.com) and sometimes a FQDN — should feed known_hostnames / known_domains and known_users
227 PASV reply reveals server-side (often internal RFC1918) IP that should be added as a host fact for topology mapping
AUTH TLS certificate CN/SAN (once negotiated) should feed hostnames/domains — the module never negotiates so this sink is starved
a passing ftp-bounce (or bounce-loopback) probe should register the server as a relay_target for internal port-scanning / firewall bypass
any files retrieved (once mirror-loot is implemented) that match /etc/shadow, SAM, wp-config, id_rsa should be parsed and posted into hashes / known_credentials
CWD-user-enum successes should push validated usernames into known_users so downstream Kerberos/SMB/RDP brute uses them
vendor identification from HELP/SITE HELP (CrushFTP, Serv-U, WS_FTP) should refine the product/version fact even when the banner was stripped by the sysadmin
priority_gaps: ftp_bounce_active_probe — one probe converts an FTP target into an internal-network relay (relay_targets fact) and firewall-bypass port-scanner; nothing comparable elsewhere in the tool
credential_brute_force_and_defaults — anon is the only auth attempt today; add default-creds sweep and password-spray using known_users / known_credentials facts (huge foothold ROI)

recent_vendor_cves_missed — banner map is stuck in 2011-2015; missing CrushFTP CVE-2024-4040, Serv-U CVE-2021-35211 / CVE-2024-28995, WS_FTP CVE-2023-40044, ProFTPD CVE-2019-12815 — all currently exploited in the wild
active site_cpfr_cpto probe + mirror_content_hash_extraction — turn 'we can read/write' into hashes/creds/config files that fan out to the rest of the fact graph
summary: The FTP module is a competent credential-free triage layer (banner-based backdoor map, anonymous-login check, FEAT-only AUTH-TLS posture, and a reversible STOR/DELE write proof) but stops well short of what RFC 959/2228/2389/2428/3659/4217 and modern FTP-server CVE research make available. The biggest missing primitives are: FTP bounce (active PORT-relay probe, would feed relay_targets), an actual credential attack surface (only 'anonymous' is tried — no default-creds sweep, no password-spray, no reuse of known_credentials), active SITE HELP / SITE CPFR probing (banner-only mod_copy detection misses many patched-banner installs of CVE-2015-3306 / CVE-2019-12815), real AUTH TLS negotiation (currently only checks FEAT text — no cert capture, no weak-cipher / CCC / PROT-not-enforced detection), and a modern CVE catalog for CrushFTP (2024-4040), Serv-U (2021-35211), WS_FTP (2023-40044) and ProFTPD (2019-12815, 2020-9273). Cross-service wiring is thin: anon success does not emit a working credential, SYST/banner os_hint is not published, PASV internal-IP leaks and TLS cert CN/SAN never reach hostnames/domains, and although a mirror runbook is printed, nothing actually retrieves files or extracts hashes from them.
notes: Confirmed test coverage in tests/test_service_fidelity.py (anonymous+cleartext detection, vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor banner match, multi-service host enumeration) and tests/test_hostile_server_fidelity.py (probe survives hostile responses). No tests exist for PASV parsing, SITE HELP, FTP bounce, TLS negotiation, or credential brute — confirming these code paths are absent, not merely untested.
